title: Five Pathways to a Blue Career: SKILLS Summer Schools Coming to Puglia in 2027
excerpt: From sustainable aquaculture to marine plastics and island energy systems, five selected Summer School proposals will shape the SKILLS learning offer in Puglia in 2027. Discover the themes—and follow the next announcements for participation details.
body:
What connects a healthier coastline, a new product made from marine plastic waste and an island powered by renewable energy? They all need people with the knowledge and skills to turn ideas into solutions.

As senior advisor to the SKILLS project, I am pleased to share a milestone: Regione Puglia has completed the selection of five Summer School proposals from the University of Bari, Politecnico di Bari and the University of Salento, connecting higher education with the challenges and opportunities of the South Adriatic blue economy. In 2027, they will form a coordinated cross-border learning offer under Activity A.3.2, which supports higher education learning modules and blue career pathways for students.

Five themes, a shared ambition

The selected proposals explore different ways to build a more sustainable and innovative relationship with the sea:

  • South Adria Coast — University of Bari: How can we better monitor and manage our coastlines? This programme focuses on legal and ecological tools for managing the Southern Adriatic coastal zone and its assets, within the framework of the EU Strategy for the Adriatic and Ionian Region, EUSAIR.

  • Recycling Materials from Plastic Waste — REMAPLA — Politecnico di Bari: What if marine plastic waste could become a resource? The programme explores sustainable management, recycling and the transformation of plastic waste into raw materials and new products.

  • AQUADIVERS — University of Bari: How can aquaculture respond to future needs? This programme focuses on sustainable aquaculture, including the reproduction and rearing of new fish species.

  • Renewable Energy Community of Islands — RECI — Politecnico di Bari: What would greater energy autonomy mean for an island? The programme examines isolated and island energy systems, energy planning and renewable energy sources.

  • Sea Skills — University of Salento: Which skills will help the South Adriatic blue economy adapt and thrive? This programme connects green, digital and energy transitions with marine ecosystem protection and the competitiveness of maritime and coastal supply chains.

Photo: Students in the laboratory of the Institute of Marine Biology, University of Montenegro during summer school in Kotor, July 2026.

Learning across borders

The five proposals share a common purpose: helping students connect academic knowledge with the challenges facing coastal communities, marine ecosystems and blue economy businesses.

Through this coordinated offer, SKILLS aims to strengthen cross-border learning and support students as they explore future careers across the South Adriatic.

What happens next?

Regione Puglia is finalising the administrative procedures and expenditure commitments. Further announcements will provide details about partnerships, dates, venues, participant selection and the arrangements for in-person and remote learning.

Interested in building your blue career? Contact me for the next updates on the Puglia Summer Schools in 2027.
